description.value: The study investigated brain activation and heart rate variability as markers of autonomic function during paced breathing, psychosocial stress induction, and stress recovery.

design.value: Each participant underwent a single MRI-scanning session while performing a paced-breathing and stress-induction task. The study combined whole-brain fMRI, continuous photoplethysmography and respiration measurements, HRV analyses, fMRI activation contrasts, physiological regressors, psychometric regressions, generalized additive models, and Granger causality analyses.

description.value: We recruited 35 healthy participants through community advertisements. Three participants were excluded due to excessive head movement during scanning (> 4 mm, ± 3° of rotation), leading to a sample size of N = 32.

inclusion_criteria.value: no neurological disorder or head injury

exclusion_criteria.value: excessive head movement during scanning (> 4 mm, ± 3° of rotation)

medical_condition.value: no neurological disorder or head injury

task_description.value: The task began with 4 min of unpaced breathing, followed by 4 min of normal paced breathing at 10 breaths/min and 4 min of deep-paced breathing at 5.5 breaths/min. Participants then completed a modified Montreal Imaging Stress Task involving arithmetic problems and negative social evaluation, followed by a 4 min recovery-from-stress block of deep breathing at 5.5 breaths/min.

presentation_software.value: Presentation V18 (Neurobehavioral Systems, Berkeley, Calif., USA)

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to follow a paced breathing exercise. During the stress task, they had to solve simple arithmetic tasks and submit their response via a response button box.

stimuli.value: Visual breathing cues, simple arithmetic problems, feedback on submitted responses, and a mock performance bar showing manipulated relative performance.

model_settings.value: Natural log-corrected IBI and RMSSD values were compared across the experimental blocks.

software.value: GraphPad Prism version 10.0.0 (GraphPad Software, Boston, Massachusetts, USA)

model_settings.value: Post hoc comparisons of IBI and RMSSD values across different blocks.
Exploratory two-tailed correlations between differences in IBI and RMSSD across experimental conditions and PSS, TICS-SCSS, and STAI scores; P < 0.05.

A block-design model was constructed with task events modeled using boxcar functions and a 480 s high-pass filter to remove low-frequency noise and signal drift. Individual contrast images were constructed for Relaxation, Stress Reactivity, Stress Recovery Specific Relaxation, Post Stress Relaxation, stress induction versus unpaced breathing, and stress induction versus normal-paced breathing.

One-sample T-tests were employed for each of the four contrasts of interest. Whole-brain results used a cluster-defining voxel-wise threshold of FWE-corrected P < 0.05 and minimal cluster size k > 10, with cluster-level FWE-corrected P < 0.05. Stress Reactivity used a cluster-defining voxel-wise threshold of FWE-corrected P < 0.0001 and exclusive masking with stress induction versus unpaced breathing and stress induction versus normal-paced breathing.
First-level results from each subject with and without inclusion of IBI or RMSSD regressors were compared. HRV time series were resampled at the fMRI TR using a sliding-window approach.

model_type.value: one-sample T-test with individual scale scores as regressors of interest

model_settings.value: For each of the four contrasts of interest, additional one-sample T-tests included individual PSS and TICS-SCSS scores as regressors of interest; STAI scores were also tested.

Separate models predicted RMSSD and IBI using brain activation time series from seven a priori ROIs as smooth terms. Experimental condition, subjects, and time points were included as parametric terms. Thin plate regression splines modeled non-linear effects, smoothing parameters were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood (REML), and subject and condition were included as fixed effects in the final models.

model_type.value: vector autoregressive model and Granger causality analysis

model_settings.value: For each HRV–ROI pair, bivariate VAR models were fitted. Optimal lag order was determined using the Akaike Information Criterion. Significance was assessed with 1,000 permutations generated by independently shuffling HRV and ROI time series across time points; empirical P-values were Bonferroni corrected.

A 4 min recovery-from-stress block of deep breathing at 5.5 breaths/min.
